sections.section_title: Recognizing Severe Anaphylaxis and the Clinical Problem of Multiphasic Reactions
sections.description: This section introduces the core clinical syndrome in the case: severe anaphylaxis progressing to anaphylactic shock after first exposure to clarithromycin. It teaches how to recognize anaphylaxis at the bedside, clarifies the definitions of biphasic, multiphasic, refractory, and sustained anaphylaxis, and frames why recurrent episodes after apparent recovery create a distinct diagnostic and management challenge.
subtopics: Clinical definition of anaphylaxis: rapid-onset multisystem hypersensitivity with airway, breathing, circulation, and skin/mucosal involvement

sections.section_title: Immediate Emergency Management: First-Line Therapy, Supportive Care, and Early Disposition
sections.description: This section explains the acute treatment decisions made in the emergency department and early hospital course. It emphasizes epinephrine as the primary therapy, reviews adjunctive treatments and monitoring, and uses the case to discuss practical issues such as auto-injector dosing, fluid resuscitation, oxygen, and when ICU-level observation becomes necessary.
subtopics: Initial stabilization priorities: airway, breathing, circulation, and trigger removal

Escalation triggers in this case: recurrent shock, repeated epinephrine requirement, and ICU transfer

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Reasoning During Recurrence: Interpreting Relapse, Guideline Gaps, and Therapeutic Uncertainty
sections.description: This section focuses on the clinical reasoning that followed the patient's repeated relapses. It explores how clinicians distinguished multiphasic anaphylaxis from ongoing allergen absorption or refractory disease, why repeated intramuscular epinephrine remained appropriate, and how the case illustrates unresolved questions around corticosteroids, observation periods, and pre-emptive epinephrine infusions.
subtopics: Chronology of the four anaphylactic episodes over the first 12 hours

sections.section_title: Searching for Predisposition: Tryptase Testing, Mast Cell Disorders, and Suspected Systemic Mastocytosis
sections.description: This section teaches the workup for unusually severe or prolonged anaphylaxis, using the case to introduce serum tryptase interpretation and the evaluation for underlying mast cell disease. It explains why persistent tryptase elevation raised concern for systemic mastocytosis, reviews the WHO diagnostic framework, and discusses why the patient remained a probable but unconfirmed case.

sections.section_title: Recovery, Long-Term Prevention, and Clinical Lessons for Practice
sections.description: This final section covers the patient's outcome and translates the case into practical learning points for future care. It reviews discharge planning, secondary prevention, patient education, and broader lessons about anaphylaxis systems of care, including dosing, observation, and the need for better evidence and registries for complex cases.
subtopics: Clinical resolution, step-down from ICU, and discharge after 3 days
